s: The LLM-specific configuration and routing layer within an AI gateway that handles model selection, prompt caching, token budgeting, and provider-specific protocol translation.
w: Extends the base ai_gateway with LLM-specific intelligence. Manages model registry with capabilities, pricing, and context limits. Translates between unified API and provider-specific formats (OpenAI chat completions, Anthropic messages, Cohere generate). Implements prompt caching using prefix matching or semantic similarity. Enforces token-level budgets (input + output tokens separately). Supports streaming with SSE pass-through and token counting in real-time. Provides model fallback chains when primary provider is degraded or rate-limited.
use: Multi-provider deployments where application code should not know provider details
Cost optimization through prompt caching and intelligent model routing
Token budget enforcement preventing runaway spend on agentic workloads
A/B testing and gradual rollout of new model versions
avoid: Single-model deployments with one provider (direct API is simpler)
Workloads where prompt caching is not applicable (highly dynamic prompts)
Scenarios requiring sub-10ms added latency where gateway overhead matters

props.prompt_cache_ttl: How long cached prompt responses remain valid
props.model_selection_strategy: How to pick model: cheapest, fastest, highest quality, or round-robin

pat.d: Identify shared prompt prefixes across requests and cache the KV computation server-side, reducing TTFB for common system prompts.
If primary model returns 429 or 503, automatically retry with next model in priority list within latency budget.

pits: Stale cache serving outdated responses - implement TTL and invalidation for prompt caches
Token counting mismatches between gateway and provider causing budget overruns
Streaming latency added by per-chunk processing - use zero-copy pass-through where possible
tips: Prompt caching is highest-ROI optimization for LLM gateways - most workloads share system prompts
Track input vs output token costs separately - output tokens are typically 3-4x more expensive
Use model selection to match task complexity: small model for classification, large for complex reasoning
